messages.content: 計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user says: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate the standard deviation for a null hypothesis test? Actually they give sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40, population mean 98.6. They want to compute the standard deviation for the null hypothesis test? Possibly they want to compute the standard error? Or maybe they want to compute the p-value? The user says "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" That is Chinese: "Calculate the standard deviation for a null hypothesis test with sample mean 98.2, standard deviation 1.4, sample size 40, to get population mean 98.6." Actually they might want to compute the standard error of the mean difference? Or compute the standard deviation of the sampling distribution? The standard error of the mean is sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). That would be 1.4 / sqrt(40) = 1.4 / 6.3249 = 0.2215. But they mention "零假設檢定的標準差" which might refer to the standard deviation of the sampling distribution under the null hypothesis? That is the standard error of the mean difference between sample mean and population mean? Actually the standard error of the difference between sample mean and population mean is sqrt((sample_std_dev^2 / sample_size) + (population_std_dev^2 / population_size)). But we don't have population std dev. So maybe they want to compute the standard error of the sample mean difference? Actually the standard error of the sample mean difference from population mean is just the standard error of the sample mean: sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). So that is 0.2215. But the user might want to compute the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under the null hypothesis. That is indeed the standard error. So answer: 0.2215.

But the user might want to compute the p-value? They didn't ask for p-value. They asked "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" That is ambiguous. But likely they want to compute the standard error. So answer: 0.2215.

We can also compute the t-statistic: (98.2 - 98.6) / (1.4 / sqrt(40)) = (-0.4) / 0.2215 = -1.805. But they didn't ask for t-statistic. They asked for standard deviation. So answer: 0.2215.

We can also compute the p-value: For two-tailed test, degrees of freedom = 39. t = -1.805. p-value ~ 0.078. But they didn't ask for p-value. So answer: 0.2215.

Thus we respond: The standard error of the mean difference is 0.2215. If you want the t-statistic: -1.805. If you want the p-value: ~0.078. But we only answer the standard deviation. So answer: 0.2215.
